sections.content: Use *desde* *hace* + a period of time to say how long an activity or situation has continued up to the present. With a present situation, Spanish commonly uses the present tense: *Estudio* *español* desde hace un *año*. In this unit, you will also connect duration with the pretérito perfecto when describing recent experiences: He estudiado mucho desde hace un año. The key point is that desde hace is followed by a duration, such as *tres* *meses*, *dos* años or una *semana*.

items.spanish: Estudio español desde hace un año.
items.english: I have been studying Spanish for a year.

items.spanish: Vivo en Hanói desde hace tres meses.
items.english: I have lived in Hanoi for three months.

items.spanish: He practicado español desde hace una semana.
items.english: I have practised Spanish for a week.

items.spanish: Hemos hablado desde hace dos horas.
items.english: We have been talking for two hours.

sections.content: After *desde* *hace*, always supply a length of time — *tres* *meses*, *dos* años, una *semana* — never a specific point on the calendar; naming a fixed moment is desde's job alone.
